talks.title: Dillmeier Glass PPE Toolbox Talk
talks.body:
DILLMEIER GLASS COMPANY

TOOLBOX TALK  |  PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)

DATE: ____________________

DEPARTMENT: ____________________

LEADER: ____________________

WHY PPE MATTERS

PPE helps protect you from hazards created by glass, metal, equipment, and production activities. Required PPE must be worn by everyone in production areas—regardless of job title or visitor status—and whenever a task or hazard assessment requires it.

KNOW WHAT TO WEAR

EYES & HEAD

Wear ANSI-compliant eye protection in production areas, while operating forklifts, handling glass, and during specified exterior work. Hard hats/protective headgear are required in production and construction areas and when operating forklifts.

HANDS & ARMS

When handling glass or metal, wear cut-rated hand protection (minimum A4) covering the palm, back of hand, wrist, and fingers. When handling glass, wear the required cut-rated arm protection (minimum A4) if you do not regularly handle annealed glass.

ANNEALED GLASS

Employees who regularly handle annealed glass must wear a cut-rated long-sleeve shirt (minimum A5) and cut-rated chaps/leg protection (minimum A4) while in production areas or handling glass, wherever the work occurs.

FEET & SPECIALTY

Production-area footwear must cover the entire foot. Protected-toe footwear is required for people handling glass, using cranes, or working close to glass handlers. Visitors/non-employees must wear a high-visibility vest in production areas.

BEFORE YOU START

Inspect PPE at the beginning of each shift. Check usability, function, cleanliness, durability, snug fit, and that it does not interfere with movement.

Do not use PPE that is defective, damaged, or unsafe. Remove it from service for disposal, cleaning, or repair.

Clean and maintain your PPE. Clean shared PPE (such as face shields) before and after each use.

Wear a face shield together with eye protection when grinding or cutting metal.

Do not wear gloves where a documented hazard analysis identifies a reasonable risk of the glove being caught in moving machinery or materials.

Ask your supervisor if you are unsure which PPE is required for a task. Specialty PPE may be required for electrical, fall, chemical, hot-work, respiratory, or other hazards.

TALK IT THROUGH

Ask the team: What PPE is required for the job we are doing today? Is any of your PPE damaged, dirty, ill-fitting, or missing?

KEY TAKEAWAY

Wear the right PPE, inspect it before use, and replace unsafe equipment. If the hazard or PPE requirement is unclear, stop and ask your supervisor.
